tips.title: Airbrushing Vallejo Model Air — Thin Consistently
tips.text: Vallejo Model Air is thinner than Model Color and requires consistency testing. Mix 1 part Model Air with 1 part Vallejo Airbrush Thinner, adding 2-3 drops of Vallejo Flow Improver per 10 drops of thinned paint. Airbrush at 1.5-2.0 bar pressure. Test consistency on a white plastic spoon; adjust ratio or pressure until paint spreads evenly.

tips.title: Base Coat Technique with Tamiya Spray Cans
tips.text: For a solid base coat, prime your model first with Tamiya Fine Surface Primer. Apply Tamiya Spray Paints in even, overlapping layers at a 6-8 inch distance. Start horizontally along the model's length, then vertically for complete coverage. Allow 15 minutes between coats. Lightly sand with 1200-grit sandpaper between coats for a smooth finish.

tips.title: Camouflage Masking with Eduard Masks
tips.text: Use Eduard's pre-cut masking sets for intricate camouflage patterns. Apply Eduard Liquid Masking Solution to prevent silvering. Carefully apply masks, pressing down gently with a soft brush to avoid creases. Apply paint with an airbrush, starting with lighter colors. Remove masks after 24 hours for clean lines.

tips.title: Applying AK Interactive Washes — Slow and Steady
tips.text: AK Interactive Washes are concentrated; dilute with AK Interactive Thinner at a 1:1 ratio for better control. Apply with a soft brush or dropper, working from top to bottom, allowing the wash to flow into panel lines and recesses. Wipe off excess with a damp cloth or cotton swab after 10-15 minutes. Allow to dry completely before handling.

tips.title: Chipping with Sponge Technique — Controlled Weathering
tips.text: For chipping effects, lightly dab a natural sea sponge in Vallejo Model Color (mixed with a touch of Vallejo Medium), then gently tap on the model's edges and raised details. Vary pressure for different chip sizes. Use a wider, softer sponge for larger chips. Clean sponge between uses with water and mild detergent.
